correctness.rationale: For the specified centered iid Sato–Tate coefficients X_h, fixed closed 1/2-Hölder target g with real normalized Fourier coefficients beta_h in [-1,1], and 0<epsilon<=1/4, take M=ceil(A_L epsilon^-2 log(2/epsilon)). Kyselov's exact Fejér approximation gives ||q_M-g||<=C L/sqrt(M) and independent high-frequency expected sup norm O(sqrt(log M/M)). For each b in [-1,1], sliding a length-delta interval inside [b-delta,b+delta] makes its Sato–Tate conditional expectation exactly b with mass >=c delta uniformly because the density is positive on [-5/4,5/4]. On dyadic frequency block 2^(j-1)<|h|<=2^j, choose widths delta_j=d 2^(-3(J-j)/4); conditioned errors are independent, centered, bounded. The negative log event probability is O(sum 2^j(1+J-j))=O(M); Hoeffding plus a Bernstein grid and summing blocks yields expected centered sup norm O(sqrt(log M/M)). Markov gives positive conditional probability of small error, and the independent tail plus X0 window cost only an additional factor c epsilon. Thus probability >= exp[-C_L epsilon^-2 log(2/epsilon)] for the same target class, genuinely improving Kyselov's log-squared exponent. I separately verified symmetric frequency counts, conditional window centering and dyadic geometric cost scaling; these bounded checks are not proof of the stochastic uniform estimates, whose bounds were reconstructed analytically.
